clue.text: Sentimental jerk in Italy?

parts.note: someone from Rome, the Italian capital, is a Roman; the query marks the indirect hint
a tic is an involuntary jerk of a muscle

explanation.surface: A soppy fool spotted somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like a noun for a fool, but it is a twitch; the pieces go in answer order with the Italian part first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone given to tender, idealised feelings about love.

clue.text: It's not late when one takes a fellow in

indicators.note: with 'in', the word one takes another word inside itself
completes 'takes ... in': the fellow's name goes within the word one

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their punctuality by bringing a companion along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... in' puts TIM inside ONE, splitting it after ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving punctually is the opposite of being tardy, so the phrase means not late.

clue.text: The morning belongs to us for love-affair

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning hours
something that belongs to us is ours, so the possessive our

explanation.surface: A couple claim the morning for their romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan-word is used in English for a romance, often a secret one.

clue.text: In a difficult situation, use hose on grass

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass

explanation.surface: A gardener in trouble resorts to watering the lawn with a hosepipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests a garden hosepipe and 'grass' a lawn; both are slang senses: legwear and cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward predicament is idiomatically a tight corner or tricky position.

clue.text: Firm has deficit — one in large figures

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a deficit in accounts is a loss
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A company reports a shortfall involving one of its big statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a giant statue, like the one that stood at Rhodes.

clue.text: Crafty move before close of play

parts.note: to shift is to move

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from play

explanation.surface: A cunning manoeuvre made just before the end of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A crafty person looks evasive and untrustworthy, the sense of a sly, furtive character.

clue.text: Romantic agent taking in work

indicators.note: the spy word takes the work word inside itself

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A sentimental secret agent takes on a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts OP inside SPY, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy means mushily sentimental, the gushy side of being romantic.

clue.text: Let client change mind

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are told to change into a new order

explanation.surface: A customer is allowed to change their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellect is the reasoning faculty, the thinking mind.

clue.text: Just keep going when there's no more credit available

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
something finished and no more is over

explanation.surface: A shopper is told to carry on once their account is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over idles steadily, so the phrase means carry on at a minimal level.

clue.text: Severe, in a way, on offence — not the first

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym for offence is dropped

parts.note: a wrong is an offence or misdeed

explanation.surface: A harsh punishment for a crime, though not a first offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' removes W from WRONG, leaving RONG after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and strong both describe something intense or harsh, like a powerful wind.

clue.text: Oral application for beauty treatment

parts.note: a cosmetic put on the mouth rather than taken by mouth; oral sounds medical

explanation.surface: A medicine to swallow for a cosmetic course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral application' suggests something taken by mouth; it is applied to the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmetic colours the lips, a beauty product applied to the mouth.

clue.text: Times are changing for Arab states

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changing into a new order

explanation.surface: Times are changing for the Gulf countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The federation on the Persian Gulf is a group of Arab principalities, each ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Hue and cry at the town centre

parts.note: to yell is to cry out

indicators.note: the centre of the word town is its middle pair of letters

explanation.surface: A public outcry raised in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hue and cry' looks like the set phrase; 'Hue' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is a colour, and hue means colour.

clue.text: Spare locker?

parts.note: an extra device for fastening a lock, not a cupboard

explanation.definitionFit: A copy cut for a lock is a spare, and it is a thing that locks.

clue.text: Very attractive person possibly met aboard

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone gorgeous one might meet on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is slang for a gorgeous, desirable person.

clue.text: They're a blend of the main races

definitions.text: They're a blend of the main races

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the two words are mixed into new order

explanation.surface: A description of a nation as a melting pot of peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blend of' signals rearranging MAINRACES; the whole clue also describes the US melting pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The population of the United States famously mixes peoples from many origins.

clue.text: Fall that impairs vision

explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall, and also a clouding of the eye's lens that dims sight.

clue.text: Undiscovered aptitude for the double anagram

definitions.text: Undiscovered aptitude for the double anagram

parts.words: Undiscovered aptitude for the double anagram
parts.note: a hidden gift, described as a pair of words that are rearrangements of each other

explanation.surface: Someone has a gift for wordplay they never knew about.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words of the phrase use exactly the same six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift not yet revealed is dormant ability waiting to be found.

clue.text: "Bony" ran Gaul erratically

indicators.note: erratically means irregularly, so the letters run in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A thin person ran across ancient France unsteadily.
explanation.definitionFit: A bony figure is all sharp corners and lean edges.

clue.text: Sandwiches and drinks

explanation.definitionFit: A round is a sandwich made from two slices of bread, and also a set of drinks bought for a group.

clue.text: Purveyor of drinks acquired weapon during prohibition

indicators.note: the weapon word sits within, during, the prohibition word

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A bootlegger got hold of a gun in the Prohibition era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts ARM inside BAN after its first letter; 'Prohibition' suggests the US alcohol ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A man serving at a bar sells drinks.

clue.text: They may be held in revulsion

definitions.text: They may be held in revulsion

parts.words: They may be held in revulsion
parts.note: held suggests regard, but here people physically hold their ... against a stink

explanation.definitionFit: People pinch their nostrils shut at a disgusting smell.

clue.text: Suspect behaviour of an absconding child

parts.note: someone absconding is going, leaving
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Questionable conduct by a runaway youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady activities or dubious happenings are idiomatically called carryings-on.

clue.text: A lot may go when it falls

definitions.text: A lot may go when it falls

parts.words: A lot may go when it falls
parts.note: a lot is an auction item, sold when the auctioneer's hammer comes down

explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's hammer marks a sale with a knock.

clue.text: Girl secures employment as baggage carrier

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the employment word securely within it

parts.note: Carol is a girl's name
employment is use

explanation.surface: A woman finds a job at an airport luggage belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' puts USE inside CAROL, after CARO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating airport belt delivers passengers' luggage.

clue.text: Notice a split coming

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
a vent is a slit or opening, as in the back of a jacket

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tear forming.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival, the coming of something.

clue.text: Short data about university's ranking

indicators.note: the data word goes around the university letter

parts.note: stats is short for statistics, data
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Brief figures on a university's league table position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts U inside STATS before the last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Uneasy, lacking support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue in snooker
less as a suffix means lacking or without

explanation.surface: Someone feels anxious with nothing to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix comes after the support word even though 'lacking' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person is fidgety and ill at ease.
